questions.title: What ischaemic heart disease is
questions.question: The following is true about ischemic heart disease (IHD):

options.A: It is due to embolism of the coronary arteries in more than 90% of cases.
options.B: It represents a group of syndromes resulting from myocardial ischaemia.
options.C: Sudden coronary occlusion always causes sudden death.
options.D: Posterior infarctions are the most common types of myocardial infarction.

explanations.A: Incorrect. In more than 90% of cases IHD is due to coronary ATHEROSCLEROSIS, not embolism; emboli are a rare cause.
explanations.B: Correct. Ischaemic heart disease is not a single entity but a GROUP OF SYNDROMES (angina pectoris, acute myocardial infarction, chronic ischaemic heart disease/heart failure and sudden cardiac death) that all result from an imbalance between myocardial oxygen demand and coronary blood supply, i.e. MYOCARDIAL ISCHAEMIA. The underlying cause in the great majority is coronary atherosclerosis. Grouping these syndromes under one heading reflects their shared ischaemic mechanism.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Sudden coronary occlusion does not ALWAYS cause sudden death; outcome ranges from angina to infarction to sudden death depending on collaterals, site and extent.
explanations.D: Incorrect. ANTERIOR wall infarctions (left anterior descending territory) are the commonest, not posterior.

questions.learning_objective: Define ischaemic heart disease as a group of syndromes resulting from myocardial ischaemia.

questions.hold: morphology of MI: more than one option is defensibly true (coagulative necrosis after 24h, fibrous scar over 2-3 months, phagocytosis/organisation in the first week) and the printed red key could not be resolved to a single option; render did not disambiguate this pass.

questions.title: The cause of IHD in >90% of cases
questions.question: Ischemic heart disease, in more than 90% of the cases, is due to:

options.B: Coronary stenosis due to syphilitic aortitis

explanations.A: Incorrect. Coronary emboli (e.g. from infective endocarditis or mural thrombi) are a rare cause of IHD, not the >90% cause.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Syphilitic aortitis can narrow the coronary ostia but is a rare, historical cause, not the dominant one.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Coronary spasm (e.g. Prinzmetal angina) contributes in a minority and often on top of atherosclerotic plaque; it is not the >90% cause.
explanations.D: Correct. In more than 90% of cases ischaemic heart disease is caused by CORONARY ATHEROSCLEROSIS, which narrows the coronary lumen and, on plaque rupture with superimposed thrombosis, precipitates acute ischaemia and infarction. The other listed mechanisms (emboli, spasm, syphilitic ostial stenosis) are individually uncommon. Atherosclerotic coronary artery disease is therefore essentially synonymous with IHD in practice.

questions.learning_objective: State that coronary atherosclerosis causes IHD in more than 90% of cases.

questions.title: The catastrophic form of IHD
questions.question: The catastrophic form of ischemic heart disease is:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Angina pectoris is transient reversible ischaemia (chest pain relieved by rest/nitrates) without myocyte death, not the catastrophic form.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Ischaemic cardiomyopathy is the chronic, progressive end-stage of IHD (heart failure), not the acute catastrophic event.
explanations.C: Correct. MYOCARDIAL INFARCTION is the catastrophic (acute, potentially fatal) form of ischaemic heart disease: prolonged occlusion causes irreversible ischaemic (coagulative) necrosis of myocardium, with the risk of arrhythmia, cardiac failure, rupture and sudden death. It is distinguished from angina by the presence of actual muscle death. This makes it the most dangerous of the IHD syndromes.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Toxic myocarditis is inflammatory myocardial injury from toxins, not a form of ischaemic heart disease.

questions.learning_objective: Identify myocardial infarction as the catastrophic form of ischaemic heart disease.

questions.title: Chest pain with high LDL and ischaemic ECG
questions.question: A 60-year-old man suffered from attacks of severe chest pain. Laboratory investigations revealed increased serum level of LDL. ECG showed signs of inadequate coronary blood flow. The most possible diagnosis is:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Hypertension is a risk factor but does not by itself explain the raised LDL plus the ECG signs of inadequate coronary flow.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Coronary embolism is a rare cause of ischaemia and is not linked to a raised LDL profile.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Aortic stenosis can cause angina, but the raised LDL and ischaemic ECG point to atherosclerotic coronary disease as the primary lesion here.
explanations.D: Correct. Severe chest pain, a RAISED serum LDL (a major atherogenic risk factor) and ECG evidence of inadequate coronary blood flow together indicate CORONARY ATHEROSCLEROSIS producing ischaemic heart disease. LDL drives plaque formation, and the narrowed coronary lumen limits flow, giving anginal pain and ischaemic ECG changes. This clinical triad is the classic presentation of atherosclerotic coronary artery disease.

questions.learning_objective: Recognise raised LDL plus ischaemic ECG as coronary atherosclerosis causing IHD.

questions.title: Cause of sudden coronary occlusion
questions.question: Sudden coronary artery occlusion is commonly caused by:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Intimal (intraplaque) haemorrhage can enlarge a plaque but is usually a contributor to, not the direct cause of, sudden total occlusion.
explanations.B: Correct. Sudden coronary occlusion is commonly caused by THROMBOSIS superimposed on a disrupted (ruptured or eroded) atherosclerotic plaque: the exposed lipid core and collagen trigger platelet aggregation and a fibrin thrombus that abruptly occludes the lumen. This acute thrombotic occlusion is the usual trigger of acute myocardial infarction. It is the final event that converts a stable plaque into an acute coronary syndrome.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Embolism is a rare cause of coronary occlusion.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Polyarteritis nodosa is a rare vasculitis and is not a common cause of sudden coronary occlusion.

questions.learning_objective: State that thrombosis on a ruptured plaque is the common cause of sudden coronary occlusion.

questions.title: Not a complication of MI
questions.question: All are complications of myocardial infarction except:

explanations.A: Incorrect (it IS a complication). Loss of contractile myocardium causes acute (left) heart failure and, if extensive, cardiogenic shock.
explanations.B: Incorrect (it IS a complication). Mural thrombus over the infarct can embolise to the systemic circulation (brain, kidneys, spleen, limbs).
explanations.C: Incorrect (it IS a complication). Ventricular fibrillation is a major early arrhythmic complication and cause of sudden death after MI.
explanations.D: Correct (the exception). POLYARTERITIS NODOSA is a systemic necrotising vasculitis, an entirely separate immune-mediated disease; it is NOT a complication of myocardial infarction. The recognised complications of MI are arrhythmias, heart failure/cardiogenic shock, mural thrombosis with embolism, myocardial rupture, pericarditis and ventricular aneurysm. PAN does not belong to this list.

questions.learning_objective: List the complications of myocardial infarction and exclude polyarteritis nodosa.

questions.title: Not a manifestation of acute cardiac ischaemia
questions.question: The clinical manifestations of acute cardiac ischaemia include all except:

explanations.A: Incorrect (it IS acute). Unstable angina is an acute coronary syndrome caused by plaque disruption with a non-occlusive thrombus.
explanations.B: Correct (the exception). HEART FAILURE (ischaemic cardiomyopathy) is the CHRONIC manifestation of ischaemic heart disease, the progressive pump failure that follows cumulative myocardial loss, not an ACUTE ischaemic event. The acute cardiac ischaemic syndromes are unstable angina, acute myocardial infarction and sudden cardiac death. Chronic heart failure therefore stands apart from the acute group and is the exception here.
explanations.C: Incorrect (it IS acute). Sudden cardiac death, usually from a fatal arrhythmia on acute ischaemia, is an acute presentation.
explanations.D: Incorrect (it IS acute). Acute myocardial infarction is the prototypical acute ischaemic event.

questions.learning_objective: Distinguish the acute ischaemic syndromes from chronic ischaemic heart failure.
questions.author_notes: Adjudicated key: heart failure is the chronic IHD syndrome and is the odd one out among the acute presentations (unstable angina, MI, sudden death). Detector gave no single red option on this negative-stem page.

questions.title: Commonest site of MI
questions.question: The commonest site of myocardial infarction is:

explanations.A: Correct. The commonest site of myocardial infarction is the ANTERIOR WALL of the LEFT VENTRICLE (extending to the adjacent interventricular septum and apex), the territory of the LEFT ANTERIOR DESCENDING (LAD) coronary artery, which is the most frequently and severely affected coronary vessel. The left ventricle bears the greatest workload and oxygen demand, so its anterior LAD territory infarcts most often. This makes anteroseptal infarction the typical pattern.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Posterior/inferior left ventricular infarcts (right coronary or circumflex territory) are less common than anterior LAD infarcts.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The lateral wall (circumflex territory) is a less frequent site than the anterior wall.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Isolated right ventricular infarction is uncommon; the left ventricle is far more often involved.

questions.learning_objective: State that the anterior wall of the left ventricle (LAD territory) is the commonest MI site.

questions.title: False statement about acute MI
questions.question: The following statement is false about acute myocardial infarction:

options.A: Diabetic persons may have silent (asymptomatic) myocardial infarction
options.B: Elevated serum cardiac troponins is the gold standard test for diagnosis
options.C: Infarction is seen as a yellow area grossly within 4 hours after the heart attack
options.D: Earliest microscopic finding is the wavy myocardial fibres at the border of the infarction site

explanations.A: Incorrect (a true statement). Diabetics with autonomic neuropathy may have silent (painless) infarcts.
explanations.B: Incorrect (a true statement). Serum cardiac troponins (I/T) are the most sensitive and specific gold-standard biomarker for diagnosing MI.
explanations.C: Correct (the false statement). At 4 hours there is NO gross (naked-eye) change: the infarct is not visible macroscopically until about 12-24 hours, when it first appears as a pale, then yellow, area. The description of a visible yellow area within 4 hours is therefore false, because gross yellowing (with a hyperaemic border) develops over roughly 1-3 days, not in the first few hours. This time-course error is what the question tests.
explanations.D: Incorrect (a true statement). Wavy myocardial fibres at the infarct margin are among the earliest microscopic changes.

questions.learning_objective: State that gross changes of MI are not visible within 4 hours (appear ~12-24 h onward).

questions.title: IHD inversely correlated with which lipoprotein
questions.question: The incidence of ischemic heart disease is inversely correlated with the serum level of:

explanations.A: Incorrect. VLDL (triglyceride-rich) is atherogenic; higher levels tend to raise, not lower, IHD risk.
explanations.B: Incorrect. LDL is the principal atherogenic lipoprotein; its level is DIRECTLY (positively) correlated with IHD.
explanations.C: Correct. HIGH-DENSITY LIPOPROTEIN (HDL, the 'good' cholesterol) is INVERSELY correlated with ischaemic heart disease: HDL carries cholesterol away from the arterial wall back to the liver (reverse cholesterol transport), so higher HDL means fewer atherosclerotic events. Thus a high HDL is protective, and its level moves opposite to IHD risk. This inverse relationship is the point tested.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Total cholesterol (largely LDL-borne) is positively, not inversely, related to IHD.

questions.learning_objective: State that HDL is inversely correlated with ischaemic heart disease incidence.

questions.title: Not a feature of transmural MI
questions.question: The following is not a feature of transmural myocardial infarction:

options.D: Does not involve the whole thickness of the myocardium

explanations.A: Incorrect (it IS a feature). A transmural infarct is ischaemic (coagulative) necrosis of myocardium.
explanations.B: Incorrect (it IS a feature). Transmural infarction is typically caused by acute occlusive thrombosis on a ruptured coronary plaque, so it is characteristically accompanied by thrombosis.
explanations.C: Incorrect (it IS a feature). Being in the solid left-ventricular wall, it is a pale (anaemic) infarct.
explanations.D: Correct (the exception). By definition a TRANSMURAL infarct extends through the FULL (whole) thickness of the ventricular wall, from endocardium to epicardium. Saying it 'does not involve the whole thickness' describes a SUBENDOCARDIAL (non-transmural) infarct instead, so this statement is false for transmural MI. Full-wall involvement is precisely what the word transmural means.

questions.learning_objective: State that a transmural infarct involves the full wall thickness (endocardium to epicardium).

questions.title: When the fibrous scar of MI appears
questions.question: In myocardial infarction, the fibrous scar appears after:

explanations.A: Incorrect. At 1-3 days there is coagulative necrosis with neutrophil infiltration, not scarring.
explanations.B: Incorrect. At 4-7 days macrophages are removing dead myocytes; granulation tissue is only beginning, not a fibrous scar.
explanations.C: Incorrect. At 1-2 weeks well-developed granulation tissue with early collagen is present, but a dense fibrous scar has not yet formed.
explanations.D: Correct. The dense collagenous FIBROUS SCAR of a healed myocardial infarct is established over roughly 2-6 WEEKS (with maturation continuing towards about 2 months): granulation tissue laid down in the second week is progressively replaced by collagen. This late fibrous replacement marks the healed stage of infarction. Hence the scar appears after about 2-6 weeks, not in the first days.

questions.learning_objective: State that the fibrous scar of MI forms over about 2-6 weeks.

questions.title: Not a feature of healed MI
questions.question: The following may be features of healed myocardial infarction except:

explanations.A: Incorrect (it IS a feature). A thin fibrous scar can bulge to form a ventricular (cardiac) aneurysm, a recognised feature of healed MI.
explanations.B: Correct (the exception). An INCREASED serum CPK (and troponin) is a marker of ACUTE myocyte necrosis; these enzymes rise and then normalise within days of the acute event. In a HEALED infarct (scar tissue), there is no ongoing necrosis, so cardiac enzymes are NORMAL, not raised. A persistently elevated CPK is therefore not a feature of a healed MI.
explanations.C: Incorrect (it IS a feature). The fibrous scar disrupts conduction and is a substrate for chronic arrhythmias.
explanations.D: Incorrect (it IS a feature). Loss of functioning myocardium leads to chronic (congestive) heart failure.

questions.learning_objective: State that raised serum CPK marks acute (not healed) MI; scar-related aneurysm, arrhythmia and failure are healed-MI features.
